answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and records equivocation correlations across the consensus graph. If k identities coordinate conflicting votes, their aggregate penalty grows as O(k^2), making collusion more costly than isolated faults. Detection then applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the swarm, with asymmetric depreciation preventing recovery. A bridge, trellis, and vine of aliases therefore cannot dilute accountability.
